name: Carvana
description: Carvana sells used cars entirely online, with its own inspection-and-reconditioning centers (many in former ADESA auction sites), vending machines and a nationwide delivery network. Most revenue is the car itself, but a large slice of gross profit comes from selling the car loans it originates to financing partners and from commissions on service contracts, GAP and insurance, which carry a 100% gross margin ($1,733M in 2025, 41% of gross profit). It also buys cars from consumers and sells the surplus through wholesale channels and its wholesale marketplace. It sold 596,641 retail cars in 2025 (+43%) and 384,718 in the first half of 2026 (+39%). The Garcia family's DriveTime is a related party that services Carvana's finance receivables, administers its warranties and trades wholesale cars with it.

businessLines.name: Wholesale sales and revenues
businessLines.how: Sells vehicles bought from consumers at auction-style prices for a thin margin ($1,015 gross profit per wholesale unit FY2025), and takes fees from other sellers' cars run through the marketplace.
businessLines.description: Trade-ins and other acquired cars that do not fit the retail inventory, sold to wholesalers, plus wholesale marketplace fees from other sellers' cars.

businessLines.name: Other sales and revenues (finance and add-ons)
businessLines.how: Sells each loan to a financing partner or securitization at a premium over its cost, and earns a commission on each service contract, GAP and insurance policy attached to the car; both scale with retail units.
businessLines.description: Gains on sale of loans Carvana originates to finance its customers, plus commissions on vehicle service contracts, GAP waiver and auto insurance.
